note: The suggestion workbench. Each item is scored on four 1-5 dimensions by ONE documented rubric, so any reviewer can re-score it and see whether they disagree. The score is a demo prioritisation model, not a verdict: the reviewer's choice is recorded separately and is the only thing that decides. Fields that would require a fact nobody has are left null and rendered as blank.

rubric.question: Does it change a decision someone has to make this season?
rubric.scale: 1 = no decision depends on it, 5 = several blocked decisions depend on it

rubric.question: Is the underlying evidence verifiable in this repository today?
rubric.scale: 1 = would need data we have never seen, 5 = the evidence is already committed

rubric.question: How much work is it, in reverse (5 = cheapest)?
How little regulatory or reputational exposure does it add, in reverse (5 = safest)?
rubric.scale: 1 = touches money or legal scope, 5 = internal only

items.title: Write the price store at T-60 minutes, every week, automatically
items.summary: A scheduled job that snapshots every market for every game an hour before kick-off. This is the only change that unblocks closing-line value, the close-beating gate and two of the five demotion rules.
items.evidence: research/data/price_snapshots_2026.csv has 13 Week-11 games with no close, because no close exists yet; research/data/clv_ledger.csv has zero rows for the same reason.
items.cost: One scheduled workflow run per week
items.blocks_if_skipped: CLV, gate G7, demotion D1 and D5, any reward paid on signal

items.title: Settle Weeks 1-9 from the feed that already reconciles
items.summary: The results feed proves itself against the official standings and covers 136 games in Weeks 1-9. Settling the existing models against those games moves the sample from 9 bets to 1,224 and is a script, not a season of waiting.
items.evidence: research/data/results_2026.csv: 137 games, 192 standings fields reconciled with zero mismatches; research/data/results_graded_week10.csv holds the grading logic already.
items.blocks_if_skipped: Every gate with a sample-size floor, including the reward schedule

items.title: Replace the bankroll leaderboard with the signal board
items.summary: Rank on close-beating share and calibration; publish staking beside it and never combine the two. The simulation in this repository shows identical edges producing a 178-unit gain and a 16.79-unit loss under two staking rules.
items.evidence: research/data/staking_vs_signal_sim.csv; research/data/leaderboard_signal_staking.csv already carries the two blocks separately.
items.cost: A copy rule and a table change
items.blocks_if_skipped: Nothing technically, but the current board teaches the reader to rank luck

items.title: Count independent signals, not bets, when computing sample size
items.summary: Nine models whose prediction errors correlate 0.92-0.999 are closer to one signal than nine. Raw row counts flatter every result on the site, so the gates should see an effective n.
items.evidence: data/output/correlation_error.json: minimum pairwise error correlation 0.92, maximum 0.999.
items.cost: A correlation-weighted effective-sample calculation in the gate
items.blocks_if_skipped: Every claim of independent evidence in the strategy lab

items.title: Price availability by depth slot into the side
items.summary: Nine of thirteen Week-11 lines sit more than five points from the market. The most likely cause is that the model ignores who is actually playing. Adding the depth slot as a term is the direct test.
items.evidence: research/data/market_origination_wk11.csv (9 of 13 games beyond 5 points); research/data/replacement_depth_measured.csv (depth slot on 7 of 7 rows, snap share on 0).
items.cost: Needs a snap-count or playing-time source that has not been verified
items.blocks_if_skipped: The answer to why the model disagrees with the market, register C2

items.title: Resolve the two-source absence-window conflict (F-04)
items.summary: Two official NFL.com items give different absence windows for the same player. A depth table and any availability-priced line rest on that assumption, so someone has to rule on it and record the ruling.
items.evidence: flagged.html F-04; data/qb-starter-changes.csv carries both URLs side by side.
items.blocks_if_skipped: The availability term and the depth table's priceability

items.title: Publish the decision register and the suggestion workbench as the entry point
items.summary: One page that answers 'what do we know, what is missing, and what would settle it' before a reader reaches any table. This repository now has the register; the landing page should lead with it.
items.evidence: research/decision-register.md (31 questions, each with a status and an owner); review.html and suggestions.html hold the existing registers.
items.cost: A link and a paragraph on the landing page
items.blocks_if_skipped: Nothing, but the site's best content stays undiscovered

items.title: Extend the capture to parlay and prop prices
items.summary: The same odds feed that carries game lines also carries per-player targets with open and current numbers. Capturing those turns the prop and parlay questions from unanswerable into measurable.
items.evidence: The prop endpoint returned 730 targets for a single settled game, each with a current and an open value.
items.cost: An extension of the same capture job; no new provider
items.blocks_if_skipped: H5, H6 and every prop-combination question

items.title: Fix the staking rule in writing before any live run
items.summary: Flat units and proportional staking reach opposite verdicts on the same edge. Until the rule is fixed in advance, any ROI comparison can be tuned after the fact, which is the definition of hindsight in staking.
items.blocks_if_skipped: Demotion D2, gate G8, every ROI comparison

items.title: Hold every reward figure at blank until a strategy clears D1 and D2
items.summary: No reward amount is published anywhere in this repository, deliberately. Paying on a bankroll curve pays for luck, and paying on CLV is impossible until W01 ships.
items.evidence: research/data/demotion_gate_rules.csv: all five rules currently BLOCKED or NOT MET; leaderboard.html's reward amounts are blank.
items.cost: A decision to wait, which is free
items.blocks_if_skipped: The credibility of the whole competition

items.title: Run the demotion gate as a scheduled check, not a meeting
items.summary: The gate is a script over the graded dataset. Running it weekly is what makes demotion real; running it after a bad month is what makes it theatre.
items.evidence: research/data/demotion_gate_run.csv and demotion_gate_rules.csv are generated by tools/build_integrity.py.
items.cost: One line in the weekly workflow
items.blocks_if_skipped: The gate only exists on paper

items.title: Add a per-page provenance line that names the exact generator
items.summary: Every page already names its sources; the missing link is which script produced which number, so a reviewer can go straight to the formula.
items.evidence: programme.html carries the pattern in its footer; the other desk pages do not.
items.blocks_if_skipped: Nothing; it is a reviewer convenience
